Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:51: Therefore a leader, judge, or charity collector must not be a flatterer - for if he flatters someone and does not rebuke him to do good and turn from evil, then the whole community will be corrupted by him, each saying, the leader flatters so-and-so, so why should he rebuke me, since he flatters so-and-so? - and they will not accept his rebukes. And likewise a judge who flatters one of the litigants, then the words of the other will be stifled and he will not know how to argue properly, and the judgment will not come out true. And likewise charity collectors who flatter will give charity to one who flatters them, or whom they flatter, and give to him even though he is unworthy of it. Therefore the righteous person must distance himself greatly from flattery, neither flattering others nor accepting flattery from others. And he should be very careful, when he does good deeds, not to intend by them to flatter others, but to do them for the sake of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:52: And the worst of all flattery is one who flatters his fellow so as to cause him to sin - such as one who has a dispute with people and the law is not with him, and he flatters people to assist him and support his error; or one who pursues transgressions, such as licentiousness and other transgressions, and flatters his fellow so that he does likewise. Jeroboam son of Nebat merited kingship because he did not flatter King Solomon but rebuked him concerning the matter of the Millo (Sanhedrin 101b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:53: Whoever wishes to be saved from flattery should be careful to distance himself from honor, for whoever does not care about being honored will not need flattery. And he must also be careful of others, for most flatterers flatter a person from whom they suppose they will derive benefit. Therefore whoever distances himself from these two things - benefit and honor - is saved from several transgressions, for many people do good deeds in order to receive honor from people, and this matter corrupts all of a person's service - for how many people pray with a pleasant voice, and think in their heart during prayer, how pleasant is my voice and how many people enjoy hearing me - and this is the way of the evil inclination, and it does this in order to catch a person in its net so that his deeds not be for the sake of Heaven. And likewise concerning benefit - one who benefits from his fellow, even if he sees him transgressing all the transgressions in the world, will not dare rebuke him, fearing that he will no longer benefit from him. And this matter is the stumbling block of the sages of the generation, for they pursue benefit from the people, and therefore flatter them so that they hold them in great esteem - and it is not enough that they do not rebuke them concerning their affairs, but by flattering them they themselves come to hold their deeds and follow after them - to this point. Rabbeinu Moshe [Maimonides] wrote this in Hilchot De'ot.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:54: In explaining the group of liars, that is, the group of falsehood - the liar and the deceiver are hated and abhorred before the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Proverbs 6:16), "these six the LORD hates," and so on: "haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that are swift [to run to evil], a false witness who breathes out lies, and one who sows discord among brothers" - and of these seven things, three of them concern falsehood: "a lying tongue," "breathes out lies," "a false witness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:55: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said that these seven evil qualities all hang upon falsehood, from which they all cascade. How so? "Haughty eyes" - the essence of pride is falsehood, for he says he is wise when he is a fool, mighty when he is weak, a prince when he is lowly, and boasts before people with these false qualities - as Absalom said (2 Samuel 15:4), "and let everyone who has a suit or cause come to me, and I would give him justice," and he was stealing people's minds through falsehood.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:56: "A lying tongue" - falsehood itself. "And hands that shed innocent blood" - from Joab, who sent a false message in David's name and brought back Abner and killed him, as it is said (2 Samuel 3:26), "and he sent messengers after Abner," and so on. "A false witness who breathes out lies" - behold the bodies of falsehood. "And one who sows discord among brothers" - as it is said (Psalms 55:10), "swallow up, O LORD, and divide their tongue," and so on, and right after it, "wickedness and mischief are in the midst of it; deceit and guile do not depart from its streets."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:57: Come and see how they lied and were punished. Gehazi lied, and he and his seed were struck with leprosy, as it is said (2 Kings 5:25), "and Elisha said to him, where have you been, Gehazi? And he said, your servant did not go anywhere," and he said to him, "did my heart not go [with you]," and so on (5:27), "the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your seed forever - and he went out from before him leprous like snow." Amnon lied, and was killed, as it is said (2 Samuel 13:5), "let Tamar my sister come and make cakes before my eyes," and so on, "and he lay with her," and Absalom killed him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:58: And whoever falsifies in his speech is as though he worships idols, as it is said (Genesis 27:12), "perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver [metate'a]," and it is written concerning idolatry (Jeremiah 51:18), "they are vanity, a work of delusions [ta'tu'im]" (Sanhedrin 92a). And Rabbi Yitzchak Aboab explained in Sefer Menorat HaMaor (letter 37), concerning this matter, why he should be like an idol-worshipper - the intent being that because he misleads his fellow with falsehood, along these lines whoever misleads his fellow in any manner is likewise, since he resembles idols, which also mislead people by saying that they have power.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:59: Rabbi Elazar said, the Holy One, blessed be He, created everything except falsehood, which He did not create, but people invent it from their own hearts (Tanna DeVei Eliyahu Zuta, chapter 3). And we read in the Midrash: the spirit of Naboth the Jezreelite did not merit a supernal dwelling, but only because Ahab killed him, innocent blood; and it was excluded because it contemplated speaking falsehoods, as it is said (1 Kings 22:20), "who shall entice Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth [Gilead]," and so on, "and the spirit came forward and said, I will entice him," and so on, "and He said, go out" - what is "the spirit"? This is the spirit of Naboth. What is "go out"? Go out from My partition - because of the "speaker of falsehoods, who shall not be established before My eyes" (Psalms 101:7).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:60: And the sage said, a person who lies is accounted as dead, for people do not heed his word since it is his way to lie - his life and his death are equal. And they said, of blessed memory (Sanhedrin 89b), this is the punishment of a liar - that even when he speaks the truth, they do not listen to him. And when Jeremiah rebuked Israel, he rebuked them only concerning falsehood, as it is said (Jeremiah 9:4), "they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood" - falsehood became like a nature for them, and they could not depart from it, and they wearied themselves trying to bend from the way of falsehood to the way of truth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:61: Rav Huna said, we find that Israel were exiled from their land only because they transgressed this verse (Exodus 23:7), "keep far from a false matter" - and in the Book of Lamentations this is alluded to in three places. In the alphabetic acrostic of "Eichah ya'iv be-apo," the Peh precedes the Ayin - meaning, they spoke with their mouths what they had not seen with their eyes, as it is written (Lamentations 2:16), "they have opened their mouth wide against you," and afterward (2:17), "the LORD has done what He devised." And in the alphabetic acrostic of "Ani ha-gever," "they have opened their mouth wide against us" (3:46), and afterward "my eye pours down" (3:49). And in the alphabetic acrostic of "Eichah yu'am zahav," "the presence of the LORD has divided them" (4:16), and afterward (4:17), "still our eyes fail."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:62: And we read in "HaBa al Yevimto" (Yevamot 63a): Rav Huna's wife would vex him - when he told her, prepare me lentils, she prepared him chickpeas; [when he said,] chickpeas, she prepared him lentils. When his son Chiya grew up, he would reverse [the instruction to her]. He [Rav Huna] said to him, your mother has improved! He said to him, I am the one who reverses it [before giving it to her]. He said to him, this is what people say, "what comes from you teaches you" - but you should not do this, for it is said, "they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood." Therefore let a person train his tongue to speak truth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:63: And Rabbeinu Yonah wrote in Sha'arei Teshuvah (Gate 3, letter 181), that this is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 6:19), "a false witness who breathes out lies" - meaning, one accustomed to speaking falsehood even in ordinary matters, all the more so will he lie and speak falsely to testify against his fellow, because of his nature and the habit of his tongue.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:64: Rabbeinu Yonah wrote (Gate 3, letter 178) that the group of liars divides into nine parts, and the author of Menorat HaMaor, Rabbi Yisrael, peace be upon him, shortened his wording and set it at seven, in these words:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:65: The first part: a man of lies - and it is not enough that he lies, but he destroys through his lies and steals and robs, like one who denies [a debt] to his fellow, or withholds a hired worker's wages, transgressing the commandments "you shall not deny falsely" and "you shall not lie" (Leviticus 19:11) and "you shall not withhold overnight" (ibid. 19:13); and likewise one who testifies falsely against his fellow, as it is said (Exodus 20:13), "you shall not testify against your neighbor as a false witness." And included in this part is one who deceives and defrauds in trade and partnerships, and it is written (Leviticus 25:17), "you shall not wrong one another" - and the liar is called worthless [belial] and a man of iniquity, as it is said (Proverbs 6:12), "a worthless person, a man of iniquity," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:66: The second: one who lies and deceives his fellow, and there is no immediate harm in this lie, but he intends to create a cause to harm him - like a person who deceives his fellow so that he trust him and rely on him and not guard himself from him, in order to bring about loss to him - along the lines of what is said (Jeremiah 9:7), "with his mouth he speaks peace to his neighbor," and so on, and it is written right after, "shall I not punish them for these things," and so on. And this one's punishment is for three matters: for the falsehood, for the harm, and for the loss.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:67: The third: one who comes with cunning to bring about for himself his fellow's benefit - not to steal or rob his fellow, but he sets his eyes on a future benefit coming to his fellow and maneuvers with his lies until he takes it for himself. How so? Such as one who sees his fellow buying merchandise cheaply, and goes to the seller and says to the seller, I will give you more money for this merchandise, and do not worry about so-and-so, for we are partners. Or he maneuvers so that his fellow gives him gifts because of his lies - such as saying to him, I wish to buy such-and-such land that you wish to buy, and the other gives him money so that he withdraw from the land and not take it; or he says to him, I was your good advocate before the king or the minister, and anything similar to this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:68: The fourth: one who, in telling a story of things he heard, changes some of it, with no benefit to himself and no loss to his fellow - and although he does not cause loss to others, his punishment is very great, because he brazens his face and lies from his evil nature. But they permitted changing things where there is a commandment involved, and for bringing peace - as it was taught (cf. Ketubot 17a), they praise the bride before the groom and say "a beautiful and graceful bride," even though she is not beautiful. And we read in Bereshit Rabbah (100:8), it is permitted to alter [the truth] for the sake of peace, as it is written (Genesis 50:16), "your father commanded" - for we do not find that Jacob commanded this, but they said it in his name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:69: The fifth: one who tells his fellow that he will do good for him and give him gifts, and has no intention of giving him anything - this too is a great evil, and concerning this it is said (Psalms 34:14), "guard your tongue from evil." And to what is one who boasts of a false gift comparable? To many clouds and winds, and it appears that rain has come, but it does not fall - as it is said (Proverbs 25:14), "clouds and wind without rain."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:70: The sixth: one who boasts that he did good for his fellow when he did not - and it is not enough that he lies, but he steals people's minds, as it was taught (cf. Chullin 94a), it is forbidden to steal people's minds, even the mind of a gentile - and one may not sell a gentile the meat of an unslaughtered or dead animal in place of properly slaughtered meat, nor a shoe made of the hide of a dead animal in place of the hide of a slaughtered one; and a person should not show his fellow that he is opening barrels for his sake when he intends to open it for a shopkeeper; and he should not press hospitality on his fellow knowing that he will not accept it - and such matters and the like are forbidden for several reasons: because he lies, and because he steals people's minds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:71: The seventh: one who boasts of virtues he does not have - such as saying he is a prince and of noble lineage and that his ancestors were great men of the generation - and it is not enough that he is proud and exalts himself, but he lies. And concerning this King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 17:7), "excellent speech is not fitting for a boor" - meaning, it is not fitting for one who is a boor and from a lowly family to say that he is a prince and great. "How much less lying speech for a noble" - meaning, even if he is a prince and noble in his deeds, he should not lie with his lips and boast that he gives gifts to people when he has not given - and even if he did give, it is unseemly for a person to boast of his gifts, all the more so for a noble. And if people honor him with degrees of honor, such as saying of him that he is a scholar, he should say, I am not a scholar. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Jerusalem Talmud, Makkot, chapter 3, halachah 6) that one who is honored with degrees of honor fitting to be given to one who knows two tractates, when he knows only one, should say, I know only one alone - all the more so is it forbidden to boast of what one does not have - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:72: And concerning the virtue of one who speaks truth and the punishment of one who speaks falsehood, they elaborated in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 63, page 94b), in these words: what is (Psalms 145:18), "the LORD is near to all who call upon Him," and so on? For whoever calls upon Him falsely is far from Him. "Emet" [truth] - Alef at the beginning of the alphabet, Mem in the middle, Tav at the end - its tenth [i.e., tithe/essence] is Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, "emet," which is the tenth of four hundred forty-one [the numerical value of "emet"], behold the secret of forty-five. At the time Israel falsify the Torah of truth, it is said of them (Daniel 8:12), "and it cast truth to the ground" - what is "ground"? This is the Shechinah. And in exile (Isaiah 59:15), "and truth was lacking," and falsehood ruled in the world - and who is falsehood? This is Samael. At the time truth rules, falsehood departs from the world. "Emet" is at the end of words, and they are "bara Elohim la'asot" [God created to make], "bara Elohim et" [God created (the object marker)] - through it He created the world, and through it it is called, and the whole world and all the nations of the world stand upon it. But with falsehood, "it cast truth to the ground," and falsehood ruled, as it were, in its own place, which is Jerusalem - and this caused the Temple to be destroyed and returned to chaos and void, for so they established: the First Temple was destroyed and "the earth was chaos and void" (Genesis 1:2); the Second Temple was destroyed and "darkness was upon the face of the deep" (ibid.) - for truth surrounds above and below, and at the time falsehood is made, the building is destroyed, and at that time it shall not rise again - this is what is written (Isaiah 14:12), "how have you fallen from heaven, O Hillel [Lucifer], son of the dawn" - "the crown of our head has fallen" (Lamentations 5:16) - these are the supernal Heh and the lower Heh, and Vav, the central pillar, bearing both of them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:73: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in the Midrash Ve'eleh HaDevarim Rabbah (1:10): Rabbi Reuven said, and what is the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He? "Emet" [truth] - and why "emet"? "Emet" has three letters: Alef, the first of the letters; Mem, in their middle; Tav, at their end - to say, I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God (Isaiah 44:6) - to this point. And these are the words of the Tikkunim, as explained, except that it adds the matter of saying "I am the first" - it is possible that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, intended these words by the plain meaning, to teach us that whoever speaks truth shall find no addition or subtraction in his words, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "I am the first and I am the last" - for what exists of Him when He is first is Himself what He is when He is last, and there is for us neither addition nor subtraction.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:74: And according to the secret, in the Tikkunim (page 119a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that "I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God" is said with the Name of forty-three [Sag], which is Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, which has three yuds, and concerning the three yuds it is said "I am the first and I am the last" - in these words: and that which is said, "let us make," is Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud - "I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God" - three yuds testify concerning it that there is nothing above it. And this is the very same matter he explained, that what is Yud at the beginning is itself the Yud at the end, and the first Heh has not changed from the final Heh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:75: And when you examine precisely what is said in the Tikkunim in the teaching we copied, concerning the Name Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, being the tenth [essence] of truth, we shall understand the reason the Torah is called "the Torah of truth" - because it is attached to His great Name mentioned - and this is what is explained in the Zohar several times (Parashat Yitro, page 90b), that the Torah is entirely the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He. And for this reason the Torah is also called the Tree of Life, for truth is the secret of the Tree of Life - "You shall give truth to Jacob" (Micah 7:20) - and the Torah is called truth, as it is said (Psalms 111... 119:142), "and Your Torah is truth." And so truth is alluded to in the Name of forty-three [Sag], in the secret of "I am the first," and these two Names are explained in the Tikkunim as: this is the soul, and this is the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:76: And through this we shall understand the reason that one who speaks truth prolongs his days - as explained in Sanhedrin (97a) concerning that country called "the city of truth," where none of them died before their time - and it is explained there that they would not alter their speech, and once it happened that a certain sage lodged with them, Rav Tavyomi by name, and because he altered his speech in a light matter, as explained there in the Talmud, he buried two of his sons and they expelled him from among them. And the reason for the prolonging of days is that the Name Mem-Heh [45] is the watering of the tree in its arms and branches, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 17a) in the words of Elijah, and likewise the Name Sag [63] they call, in the Tikkunim, explicitly, the soul - and the intent in the Names mentioned is the Cause of causes clothed in them, as explained in the Tikkunim - it follows that he holds fast to the supernal life, which is the life of the attributes, and therefore it is fitting that he prolong his days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:77: Also, concerning the virtue of truth, the prophet explained to us in saying (Jeremiah 10:10), "but the LORD is the true God, He is the living God" - and behold, these two Names [YHVH Elohim] total "Yabak," the numerical value of the three Names Ehyeh, YHVH, Adonai, which are "I am the first" - it follows that whoever speaks truth cleaves to His blessed Name YHVH Elohim, which is a complete Name, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 213a, and Idra, Naso, page 138b), and whoever cleaves to Him cleaves to life, as it says, "He is the living God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:78: And just as the reward is great for one who speaks truth, so the punishment is great for one who speaks falsehood, as explained in the teaching of the Tikkunim, that this caused the destruction of the First and Second Temples. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in Tractate Shabbat (119b), Jerusalem was destroyed only because men of faith ceased from it, as it is said (Jeremiah 5:1), "roam," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:79: And whoever fulfills the Torah and its commandments sustains the world, whose pillar is truth, as they said (Avot, chapter 1, mishnah 17), "on three things the world stands: on judgment, on truth, and on peace." And truth is the pillar comprising everything - and when Israel do not occupy themselves with Torah and do not fulfill it, it is written (Daniel 8:12), "and it cast truth to the ground," as explained in the Tikkunim, and then Samael, called falsehood, rules - and this is "and truth was lacking." And the reason for all this is that just as it is impossible for the body to exist without a soul, so is the soul of all existing things, and the pillar that sustains them is truth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:80: And included in speaking truth is that he not speak one thing with his mouth and another with his heart, but rather that his inside be like his outside - and Scripture is precise about this (Zephaniah 3:13), "the remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies, nor shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth." And the secret of this matter is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 230a), in these words: and therefore the masters of the Mishnah established, "not the exposition is the essential thing, but the deed" - because the Holy One, blessed be He, is hidden in the secrets of the Torah, and is known through the commandments, which are His Shechinah, His image: in the manner that He is humble, His Shechinah is humility; He is pious and she is piety; He is mighty and she is might over all the nations of the world; He is truth and she is faith; He is a prophet and she is prophecy; He is righteous and she is righteousness; He is King and she is Queen; He is wise and she is wisdom; He is understanding and she is understanding; His crown is Keter and her crown is the crown of Tiferet. And therefore the Rabbis established, whoever's inside is not like his outside should not enter the study hall - in the pattern of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is "his outside," and His Shechinah "his inside" - He is the inside, within, and she is the outside, and she does not change, outwardly, from that which is inward, to make known that she is His emanation, and there is no separation there at all, for "within and without you shall overlay it." And because He, YHVH, is hidden within, He is called only by His Shechinah, Adonai - and therefore the Rabbis said, not as I am written am I called - in this world I am written with YHVH and called with Adonai, but in the World to Come I shall be written with YHVH and called with YHVH, so that mercy be from every side. And therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded the ministering angels that whoever's inside is not like his outside shall not enter this palace, in all his internal and external limbs - and therefore the verse says (Deuteronomy 18:13), "you shall be whole with the LORD your God" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:81: Behold, it is explained in this teaching the virtue of whoever's inside is like his outside in all his matters, and this is included in the attribute of truth, for He is truth and she is faith - it follows, Heaven forfend, that whoever does not speak truth and has deceit in his tongue, his inside is not like his outside, and he cuts the plantings and separates, in the secret of Atzilut, the secret of the Holy One, blessed be He, from His Shechinah - as it says (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the LORD your God." And for this reason the prophet said (Zephaniah 3:13), "the remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies." And further, concerning the punishment of one whose inside is not like his outside, they elaborate in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 235b) and further in the Tikkunim (page 128b) - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:82: Also, included in truth is fulfilling the words of Torah in deed - for if he learns and does not practice, he is not included in truth, and this is explained at the beginning of the teaching of the Ra'aya Meheimna, which says, "not the exposition is the essential thing, but the deed" - because the Holy One, blessed be He, is hidden in the secrets of the Torah, and is known through the commandments, which are His Shechinah. Further there, He is the inside and she is the outside, and she does not change, outwardly, from that which is inward, to make known that she is His emanation. It follows that whoever expounds and does not fulfill separates and shows, Heaven forfend, that what is outside in deed is not what is inside in the speech of Torah. And therefore the deed is the essential thing that indicates unification.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:83: And so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Shelach Lecha, page 163b), that truth comprises male and female, in these words: "and Jacob was a plain [tam] man" (Genesis 25:27) - the husband of that "tam" [i.e., "tamah," the female Tiferet/Shechinah] - and who is she? The secret of the Vav [tav-mem = "tam"]. And when the male and female were included together as one, then it takes all these letters, Alef, "Tam," and it is "Emet" - "You shall give truth [emet] to Jacob" - every male and female together is the completeness of everything - to this point. It follows that whoever wishes to fulfill the attribute of truth must fulfill in deed what he occupies himself with in Torah, so that he be included in "Alef-Tam" [Emet], which are male and female - and this is the secret of "and the LORD, God, is truth [emet]" (Jeremiah 10:10), that the two Names together are the secret of "emet."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:84: Also, included in the fulfillment of truth is that he strive to be steadfast in his service like a peg that does not waver, as it is written (Isaiah 22:23), "and I will fasten him as a peg in a sure place" - and truth and faith are all one matter, as explained in the teaching, "He is truth and she is faith."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:85: Now, truth is the opposite of falsehood, for one who promises and does not do is called false, because he has broken off his promise and his word - and every term of falsehood [kazav] is derived from the language of the verse, as it is written (Isaiah 58:11), "and like a spring of water whose waters do not fail [yechazvu]." Now, the attribute of truth never ceases its mercy from the world, for it is a river that goes out from Eden to water the garden (Genesis 2:10), and it says "goes out" and not "went out," for it is forever going out - and therefore Rashbi called it a river that flows and goes out and its waters never cease - see the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, page 123b). And the essence of the attribute of truth depends on Atika, as explained in the Idra (Parashat Naso, page 140b), that from there mercy never ceases - for were it conceivable, Heaven forfend, that this flow be missing, that it be "false" [yechazev] for even a moment, the world would be nullified. And likewise a person's limbs are always available for their function - the tongue to speak, the ear to hear, the feet to walk, and the other senses - and were it conceivable that the limbs be "false" and not perform their functions, the person would be nullified. And therefore the world stands upon truth, and if any sense of theirs is sometimes nullified, it is because of the person's own cause and his own falseness in his service to the Creator.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:86: And therefore it is fitting for a person to be steadfast in his service, that he never be false in it - for if he ceases, he has ceased the attribute of truth, and he is in the husk called falsehood. And it seems close, in my view, to say that this is the attribute of "kazvani" [the false one] - for what difference does it make to me whether he lies to people or lies to the Holy One, blessed be He? And it is even more fitting to punish one who lies to the Holy One, blessed be He, than one who lies to people, as it is written (Job 13:9), "will you mock Him as one mocks a man?"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:87: And I heard from my teacher, peace be upon him, that in the mouth there are thirty-two teeth, which are the thirty-two [mentions of] "Elohim" in the account of creation, which are the thirty-two paths of Chokhmah - and the account of creation is sealed with the attribute of "emet" [truth] at its beginning and at its end: at its beginning, "Bereshit bara Elohim et [the heavens]," and at its end, "bara Elohim la'asot [to make]" - to teach you that whoever lies denies the account of creation and the thirty-two paths within it, sealed with the attribute of truth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:88: And this is why we find that "emet" is mentioned six times in the account of creation, corresponding to the six extremities sealed with the Name Yud-Heh-Vav, as explained in Sefer Yetzirah (chapter 1, mishnah 12), and these are: "Bereshit bara Elohim et," "vayar Elohim et ha-or" [and God saw the light], "vayivra Elohim et ha-taninim" [and God created the sea monsters], "vayivra Elohim et ha-adam" [and God created man], "vayar Elohim et asher asah" [and God saw what He had made], "bara Elohim la'asot" [God created to make] - so wrote Rabbi Yaakov in his commentary on the delicacies he made on the Torah. It follows that whoever lies uproots himself from the six extremities sealed with the attribute of truth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:89: And whoever wishes that there be no falsehood in his speech and dealings - if he is obligated to pay by a certain time, he should extend the time from the start, so as not to turn out a liar. And I heard that concerning this it is said (Proverbs 12:19), "the lip of truth shall be established forever, but a lying tongue is but for a moment [argi'ah]" - meaning, whoever has the lip of truth, it shall be established forever, meaning that he extends the time much, so that within the extended time he complete his word. But whoever says "at this instant," "now," "tomorrow" - this is a lying tongue, the intent being that shortening the time is a lying tongue, since it is possible that his request will not come about and he will be found a liar. And I say that it is possible that for this reason the word "emet" [truth] is alluded to at the end of words and not at the beginning of words, to indicate the lengthening of time.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:90: And so, whoever wishes to fulfill the attribute of truth should not accustom his tongue to speak falsehood even in trivial matters, because of "they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood," as we read in Yevamot (63a), "Rav's wife would vex him," and so on. And not only this, but everyone who fears Heaven should fulfill with his mouth what he agreed in his heart to fulfill - "and speaks truth in his heart" (Psalms 15:2) - as Rav Safra fulfilled this matter, as explained in Makkot (24a) and Bava Batra (88a) - see there.
